memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo:
- Status: New onset episodic spinning sensation lasting <1 minute, triggered by head movements, associated nausea. Dix-Hallpike pending.
- Plan: Start betahistine 16 mg twice daily; meclizine 25 mg SOS for acute vertigo. Arrange Dix-Hallpike test and audiometry. Advise avoidance of sudden head turns, sit‑up slowly.
Due: HbA1c repeat 2025-07-10.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg BD after food
meclizine 25 mg SOS after food

memories.author: patient
memories.text: I have felt dizzy three times since yesterday when I turn to look at the shelves. Each episode lasts about 20‑30 seconds and I feel nauseous. No hearing loss or ringing.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Dix‑Hallpike test: Positive on right side – torsional up‑beating nystagmus with latency 2 seconds, lasting <1 minute. Consistent with right posterior canal BPPV.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: Audiometry (pure tone): Right ear 250‑8000 Hz thresholds within normal limits (0‑20 dB HL). Left ear normal. No sensorineural hearing loss.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo:
- Status: Improved – only two brief episodes in past month, both resolved with meclizine. No nausea.
- Plan: Continue betahistine 16 mg BD; consider taper if symptom‑free for 6 weeks. Reinforce vestibular exercises.
Due: HbA1c repeat 2025-10-12.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
betahistine 16 mg BD after food
meclizine 25 mg SOS after food

memories.author: patient
memories.text: The dizziness has been much better. I only felt a slight sway once when I reached for a high shelf, took meclizine and it settled in a minute.

memories.author: front_desk
memories.text: Appointment booked for 2025-11-03 10:30 AM with Dr Karthik Hegde (D04).

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo:
- Status: Symptom‑free for 8 weeks, no vertigo episodes.
- Plan: Attempt betahistine taper – reduce to 8 mg BD for 2 weeks, then stop. Keep meclizine SOS. Return if symptoms recur.
Due: HbA1c repeat 2026-01-15.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
betahistine 8 mg BD after food
meclizine 25 mg SOS after food

memories.author: lab
memories.text: HbA1c 5.8% (ref 4.0‑5.6%). Slightly elevated. Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 190 mg/dL (<200), HDL 45 mg/dL (>40), LDL 110 mg/dL (<130), Triglycerides 140 mg/dL (<150). TSH 2.1 µIU/mL (0.4‑4.0).

memories.author: patient
memories.text: Two days ago I felt a sudden spin while bending to tie my shoe. It lasted about 15 seconds, I felt nauseous but no vomiting. Took meclizine and it settled.

memories.author: D04
memories.text: Dix‑Hallpike test: Positive on left side – up‑beating nystagmus with latency 3 seconds, duration <1 minute. Suggests left posterior canal BPPV now.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo:
- Status: Recurrent episodes, now left‑sided. Two episodes in past week.
- Plan: Restart betahistine 16 mg BD. Add Brandt‑Daroff exercises twice daily. Meclizine SOS for acute attacks.
Due: HbA1c repeat 2026-03-10.

memories.author: D04
memories.text:
Benign positional vertigo:
- Status: Well controlled – no vertigo spells for 3 months on betahistine 16 mg BD.
- Plan: Continue current dose. Reinforce vestibular rehab. Annual lipid check due.
Due: HbA1c repeat 2026-09-15.

memories.author: lab
memories.text: HbA1c 5.6% (ref 4.0‑5.6%). Lipid profile: Total cholesterol 185 mg/dL, HDL 48 mg/dL, LDL 105 mg/dL, Triglycerides 130 mg/dL. TSH 1.9 µIU/mL.
